title: Armed Man With Weapons Cache Arrested at Trump Golf Course Before Presidential Visit
excerpt: Jeanine John Taele, 38, was found monitoring security preparations at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, days before the president's scheduled dinner there.
body:
• Jeanine John Taele, 38, was arrested Sunday after plainclothes federal agents spotted him taking photos and monitoring security-planning activities at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, California.
  • A search of his home yielded an illegally modified AR-style rifle, a .45 caliber pistol, body armor, high-capacity magazines, and notebooks containing "concerning statements."
  • Taele pleaded not guilty to multiple felony charges including carrying a concealed firearm and possession of a short-barreled rifle. Bail was set at $250,000.
  • The FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force and Secret Service are investigating, though officials say no credible threat to the community has been identified.

An armed man was arrested at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, California, on Sunday after federal agents observed him photographing and apparently surveilling security preparations at the course — two days before President Donald Trump was scheduled to attend a Republican National Committee fundraising dinner there.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department identified the suspect as Jeanine John Taele, 38, of Downey, California. The department announced his arrest on Tuesday, the same day Trump arrived in Southern California aboard Air Force One.

The Arrest

Plainclothes federal agents noticed Taele walking the golf course grounds around 3:30 p.m. on August 2, taking photos and videos and appearing to monitor "security-planning activities," according to the sheriff's department. Deputies from the Lomita Sheriff's Station responded and determined that Taele was already under investigation by the El Segundo Police Department in connection with a November 2025 robbery.

During a pat-down, deputies found a 16-round magazine loaded with hollow-point ammunition in Taele's pants pocket, according to the sheriff's department. A search of his vehicle in the golf course parking lot uncovered a loaded pistol with a round chambered and an additional magazine containing hollow-point rounds.

Taele was arrested on charges of carrying a concealed firearm and possession of prohibited ammunition.

Weapons Cache at Downey Home

The discovery prompted detectives from the Sheriff's Department Major Crimes Bureau, assigned to the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force, to obtain a search warrant for Taele's home in Downey on Monday.

https://x.com/JesseBWatters/status/2084801402077937732

"This is an active investigation. My office, along with @FBILosAngeles and @LosAngelesATF, is reviewing the evidence and will provide more information when possible."

— Bill Essayli, First Assistant U.S. Attorney, Central District of California

Investigators recovered an illegally modified AR-platform rifle, a 1911 .45-caliber pistol, an AR-platform upper receiver, body armor, high-capacity magazines, bulk pistol and rifle ammunition, two radio signal devices, and multiple notebooks containing what authorities described as "concerning statements."

On Tuesday, Taele was formally charged with manufacturing or possessing a large-capacity magazine, carrying a concealed firearm in a vehicle, and possession of a short-barreled rifle or shotgun. He was also charged with second-degree robbery in connection with the 2025 El Segundo case. He pleaded not guilty, and bail was set at $250,000.

No Credible Threat Identified — For Now

The Secret Service is investigating whether Taele posed a threat to the president, a federal law enforcement source told CNN. The source said there was no current indication he was plotting an attack, though the investigation remains ongoing.

"Currently, investigators have identified no credible threat to our communities. However, this case underscores the importance of vigilance, strong partnerships with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, and the proactive steps taken to identify and investigate suspicious activity before it can escalate."

— Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department

The FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force and Secret Service are assisting in the investigation, and officials said additional charges could follow.

Presidential Visit Proceeds

Trump arrived in Southern California on Tuesday evening as planned. He is scheduled to attend an RNC fundraising dinner at the Rancho Palos Verdes golf course, with a roundtable at 6:30 p.m. and a reception at 7:00 p.m., according to the New York Post. The president plans to highlight his administration's economic record and border policies during the visit.

The arrest comes amid heightened security around presidential events following the assassination attempt on Trump at a Butler, Pennsylvania rally in July 2024. A separate incident in March 2026 saw another armed man — wearing body armor and carrying a rifle decorated with Joker-themed phrases — arrested near the same Rancho Palos Verdes golf club.
nri_angle: The incident at Trump's California golf club underscores ongoing security concerns at high-profile presidential venues, relevant as Indian-Americans increasingly attend political fundraisers and events hosted at such locations.
